import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.31

by O. V. Mel'nikov

b) Let $G$ be a finitely generated residually finite group, $d(G)$ the minimal number of its
generators, and $\delta(G)$ the minimal number of topological generators of the profinite
completion of $G$. It is known that there exist groups $G$ for which $d(G) > \delta(G)$
(G. A. Noskov, *Math. Notes*, **33**, no. 4 (1983), 249–254). Is the function $d$ bounded on
the set of groups $G$ with the fixed value of $\delta(G) \geq 2$?

The profinite completion $\widehat{G}$ is realised here as the closure of the image of $G$ in
the product $\prod_N G/N$ of all its finite quotients (each carrying the discrete topology),
where $N$ ranges over the normal subgroups of finite index of $G$. The minimal number of
generators $d(G)$ is Mathlib's `Group.rank G`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
namespace Kourovka.«6.31»
variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

def toFiniteQuotients : G →* ∀ N : FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup G, G ⧸ N.1 :=
  Pi.monoidHom fun N => QuotientGroup.mk' N.1
blocks.docstring: The natural map from `G` to the product `∏ N, G ⧸ N` of all its finite quotients.

justification.name: Kourovka.«6.31».toFiniteQuotients

blocks.name: toFiniteQuotients

blocks.code:
def profiniteCompletion : Subgroup (∀ N : FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup G, G ⧸ N.1) :=
  (toFiniteQuotients G).range.topologicalClosure
blocks.docstring:
The profinite completion $\widehat{G}$ of `G`: the closure of the image of `G` in the
product `∏ N, G ⧸ N` of its finite quotients, where each `G ⧸ N` is discrete and the product
carries the product topology. It is a closed subgroup of a profinite group, hence a profinite
group.

justification.closest_existing_considered: ProfiniteGrp.toFiniteQuotientFunctor / ProfiniteGrp.toLimit (only for an already profinite group P), Subgroup.topologicalClosure.
justification.name: Kourovka.«6.31».profiniteCompletion
justification.why_needed: The profinite completion Ĝ, realised as the topological closure of the image of G in ∏ N, G ⧸ N (product of discrete finite groups). Mathlib has ProfiniteGrp and limits but no profinite completion of an abstract group.

blocks.name: profiniteCompletion
blocks.text:
/-- The profinite completion $\widehat{G}$ of `G`: the closure of the image of `G` in the
product `∏ N, G ⧸ N` of its finite quotients, where each `G ⧸ N` is discrete and the product
carries the product topology. It is a closed subgroup of a profinite group, hence a profinite
group. -/
def profiniteCompletion : Subgroup (∀ N : FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup G, G ⧸ N.1) :=
  (toFiniteQuotients G).range.topologicalClosure

def toProfiniteCompletion : G →* profiniteCompletion G :=
  (toFiniteQuotients G).codRestrict _ fun g => Subgroup.le_topologicalClosure _ ⟨g, rfl⟩

justification.name: Kourovka.«6.31».toProfiniteCompletion
justification.why_needed: The natural map G →* Ĝ, used for the API lemma that G is dense in Ĝ and that δ(G) ≤ d(G).

blocks.name: toProfiniteCompletion

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20 22]
theorem denseRange_toProfiniteCompletion : DenseRange (toProfiniteCompletion G) := by
  rw [DenseRange, dense_iff_closure_eq, Set.eq_univ_iff_forall]
  intro x
  rw [closure_subtype]
  have : Subtype.val '' Set.range (toProfiniteCompletion G) = Set.range (toFiniteQuotients G) := by
    ext y
    simp [toProfiniteCompletion]
  rw [this]
  exact x.2
blocks.docstring: The image of `G` is dense in its profinite completion $\widehat{G}$.
blocks.name: denseRange_toProfiniteCompletion

noncomputable def profiniteRank : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (S : Finset (profiniteCompletion G))
    (_ : (Subgroup.closure (S : Set (profiniteCompletion G))).topologicalClosure = ⊤),
    (S.card : ℕ∞)
blocks.docstring:
$\delta(G)$: the minimal number of topological generators of the profinite completion
$\widehat{G}$ of `G`, i.e. the least cardinality of a finite subset $S \subseteq \widehat{G}$
such that the subgroup generated by $S$ is dense in $\widehat{G}$. It is `⊤` if no such
finite set exists (this cannot happen when `G` is finitely generated, see
`profiniteRank_le_rank`).

justification.closest_existing_considered: Group.rank (abstract generation only, for FG groups); no notion of topological rank / topological generators in Mathlib.
justification.name: Kourovka.«6.31».profiniteRank
justification.why_needed: δ(G): the least cardinality (in ℕ∞) of a finite subset of Ĝ generating a dense subgroup, i.e. the minimal number of topological generators of the profinite completion.

blocks.name: profiniteRank
blocks.text:
/-- $\delta(G)$: the minimal number of topological generators of the profinite completion
$\widehat{G}$ of `G`, i.e. the least cardinality of a finite subset $S \subseteq \widehat{G}$
such that the subgroup generated by $S$ is dense in $\widehat{G}$. It is `⊤` if no such
finite set exists (this cannot happen when `G` is finitely generated, see
`profiniteRank_le_rank`). -/
noncomputable def profiniteRank : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (S : Finset (profiniteCompletion G))
    (_ : (Subgroup.closure (S : Set (profiniteCompletion G))).topologicalClosure = ⊤),
    (S.card : ℕ∞)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20 22]
theorem profiniteRank_le_rank [Group.FG G] : profiniteRank G ≤ Group.rank G := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨S, hS, hS'⟩ := Group.rank_spec G
  have key : (Subgroup.closure ((S.image (toProfiniteCompletion G) : Finset _) :
      Set (profiniteCompletion G))).topologicalClosure = ⊤ := by
    rw [Finset.coe_image, ← MonoidHom.map_closure, hS', ← MonoidHom.range_eq_map,
      SetLike.ext'_iff, Subgroup.topologicalClosure_coe, Subgroup.coe_top, ← dense_iff_closure_eq]
    exact denseRange_toProfiniteCompletion G
  refine (iInf₂_le (S.image (toProfiniteCompletion G)) key).trans ?_
  rw [← hS]
  exact_mod_cast Finset.card_image_le
blocks.docstring:
For a finitely generated group `G` one has $\delta(G) \leq d(G)$: the image of a
generating set of `G` topologically generates $\widehat{G}$.

def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` is residually finite if every non-identity element of `G` maps to a
non-identity element in some finite quotient of `G`, i.e. lies outside some normal subgroup of
finite index.

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.31».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.FG G],
      IsResiduallyFinite G → profiniteRank G = n → Group.rank G ≤ C := by

blocks.docstring:
Let $G$ be a finitely generated residually finite group, $d(G)$ the minimal number of its
generators, and $\delta(G)$ the minimal number of topological generators of the profinite
completion of $G$. Is the function $d$ bounded on the set of groups $G$ with the fixed value
of $\delta(G) \geq 2$?

That is: for every $n \geq 2$, is there a constant $C$ such that $d(G) \leq C$ for every
finitely generated residually finite group $G$ with $\delta(G) = n$? The value $\delta(G) = 1$
is excluded, as in the source: it forces $G$ to be cyclic, so $d(G) \leq 1$ there.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question with an implicit outer quantifier over the fixed value: for every n ≥ 2, does there exist C (depending on n) such that every finitely generated residually finite group G with δ(G) = n has d(G) ≤ C; here d(G) is the minimal number of generators (finite since G is f.g.) and δ(G) is the minimal number of topological generators of the profinite completion (equivalently, for f.g. residually finite G, the supremum of d(Q) over finite quotients Q), so δ(G) ≤ d(G) always and the case δ(G) = 1 is excluded (it forces G cyclic); Noskov's cited existence of groups with d(G) > δ(G) is background, not a question posed. Statement is the only remaining lettered part b), so the lettered-part slot rule applies.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same outer shape, which matches the decomposition reading: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 2, ∃ C, ∀ f.g. residually finite G : Type, δ(G) = n → Group.rank G ≤ C (bound depends on n, not G; G : Type loses nothing for f.g. groups; d(G) = Mathlib's Group.rank). They differ only in how δ(G) is defined. c01 defines δ(G) literally as the least size of a finite subset of the profinite completion generating a dense subgroup, where the profinite completion is built concretely as the closure of the image of G in ∏_N G/N (N over finite-index normal subgroups, each quotient discrete, product topology) — this is the standard construction and equals lim← G/N. I verified the instance resolution (coordinate topology is ⊥, Pi topology, subspace topology on the closure), and c01 additionally proves DenseRange of G → Ĝ and δ(G) ≤ d(G), which certifies the topology is right and that the ℕ∞ junk value ⊤ is unreachable under Group.FG. c05/c06 are also literal constructions but with weaker sanity lemmas (c06 via ProfiniteGrp.limit is heavier). c02/c07/c08 (δ = sup of ranks of finite quotients) and c03/c04 (δ = n as max of finite-quotient ranks) rely on the standard theorem that a profinite group is topologically n-generated iff all its finite continuous quotients are, plus the correspondence of finite quotients of Ĝ with those of G; this is true and endorsed by the decomposition notes, but the literal definition avoids baking a theorem into the definition. Only edit: one docstring sentence explaining why δ(G) = 1 is excluded. Final file compiles with only the sorry warning and passes lake --wfail build under repository linter options.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.31

by O. V. Mel'nikov

b) Let $G$ be a finitely generated residually finite group, $d(G)$ the minimal number of its
generators, and $\delta(G)$ the minimal number of topological generators of the profinite
completion of $G$. It is known that there exist groups $G$ for which $d(G) > \delta(G)$
(G. A. Noskov, *Math. Notes*, **33**, no. 4 (1983), 249–254). Is the function $d$ bounded on
the set of groups $G$ with the fixed value of $\delta(G) \geq 2$?

The profinite completion $\widehat{G}$ is realised here as the closure of the image of $G$ in
the product $\prod_N G/N$ of all its finite quotients (each carrying the discrete topology),
where $N$ ranges over the normal subgroups of finite index of $G$. The minimal number of
generators $d(G)$ is Mathlib's `Group.rank G`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.31»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- The normal subgroups of finite index of a group `G`. -/
abbrev FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup := {N : Subgroup G // N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex}

variable {G}

scoped instance (N : FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup G) : N.1.Normal := N.2.1

scoped instance (N : FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup G) : N.1.FiniteIndex := N.2.2

/-- Each finite quotient `G ⧸ N` carries the discrete topology. -/
scoped instance (N : FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup G) : TopologicalSpace (G ⧸ N.1) := ⊥

scoped instance (N : FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup G) : DiscreteTopology (G ⧸ N.1) :=
  discreteTopology_bot _

variable (G)

/-- The natural map from `G` to the product `∏ N, G ⧸ N` of all its finite quotients. -/
def toFiniteQuotients : G →* ∀ N : FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup G, G ⧸ N.1 :=
  Pi.monoidHom fun N => QuotientGroup.mk' N.1

/-- The profinite completion $\widehat{G}$ of `G`: the closure of the image of `G` in the
product `∏ N, G ⧸ N` of its finite quotients, where each `G ⧸ N` is discrete and the product
carries the product topology. It is a closed subgroup of a profinite group, hence a profinite
group. -/
def profiniteCompletion : Subgroup (∀ N : FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup G, G ⧸ N.1) :=
  (toFiniteQuotients G).range.topologicalClosure

/-- The natural map from `G` to its profinite completion $\widehat{G}$. -/
def toProfiniteCompletion : G →* profiniteCompletion G :=
  (toFiniteQuotients G).codRestrict _ fun g => Subgroup.le_topologicalClosure _ ⟨g, rfl⟩

/-- The image of `G` is dense in its profinite completion $\widehat{G}$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20 22]
theorem denseRange_toProfiniteCompletion : DenseRange (toProfiniteCompletion G) := by
  rw [DenseRange, dense_iff_closure_eq, Set.eq_univ_iff_forall]
  intro x
  rw [closure_subtype]
  have : Subtype.val '' Set.range (toProfiniteCompletion G) = Set.range (toFiniteQuotients G) := by
    ext y
    simp [toProfiniteCompletion]
  rw [this]
  exact x.2

/-- $\delta(G)$: the minimal number of topological generators of the profinite completion
$\widehat{G}$ of `G`, i.e. the least cardinality of a finite subset $S \subseteq \widehat{G}$
such that the subgroup generated by $S$ is dense in $\widehat{G}$. It is `⊤` if no such
finite set exists (this cannot happen when `G` is finitely generated, see
`profiniteRank_le_rank`). -/
noncomputable def profiniteRank : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (S : Finset (profiniteCompletion G))
    (_ : (Subgroup.closure (S : Set (profiniteCompletion G))).topologicalClosure = ⊤),
    (S.card : ℕ∞)

/-- For a finitely generated group `G` one has $\delta(G) \leq d(G)$: the image of a
generating set of `G` topologically generates $\widehat{G}$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20 22]
theorem profiniteRank_le_rank [Group.FG G] : profiniteRank G ≤ Group.rank G := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨S, hS, hS'⟩ := Group.rank_spec G
  have key : (Subgroup.closure ((S.image (toProfiniteCompletion G) : Finset _) :
      Set (profiniteCompletion G))).topologicalClosure = ⊤ := by
    rw [Finset.coe_image, ← MonoidHom.map_closure, hS', ← MonoidHom.range_eq_map,
      SetLike.ext'_iff, Subgroup.topologicalClosure_coe, Subgroup.coe_top, ← dense_iff_closure_eq]
    exact denseRange_toProfiniteCompletion G
  refine (iInf₂_le (S.image (toProfiniteCompletion G)) key).trans ?_
  rw [← hS]
  exact_mod_cast Finset.card_image_le

/-- A group `G` is residually finite if every non-identity element of `G` maps to a
non-identity element in some finite quotient of `G`, i.e. lies outside some normal subgroup of
finite index. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- Every finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/--
Let $G$ be a finitely generated residually finite group, $d(G)$ the minimal number of its
generators, and $\delta(G)$ the minimal number of topological generators of the profinite
completion of $G$. Is the function $d$ bounded on the set of groups $G$ with the fixed value
of $\delta(G) \geq 2$?

That is: for every $n \geq 2$, is there a constant $C$ such that $d(G) \leq C$ for every
finitely generated residually finite group $G$ with $\delta(G) = n$? The value $\delta(G) = 1$
is excluded, as in the source: it forces $G$ to be cyclic, so $d(G) \leq 1$ there.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.31».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.FG G],
      IsResiduallyFinite G → profiniteRank G = n → Group.rank G ≤ C := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.31»

items: The profinite completion is realised concretely as the closure of the image of G in the product ∏_N G/N of all finite quotients (N ranging over finite-index normal subgroups), each quotient discrete and the product carrying the product topology. This is the standard construction and coincides with the inverse limit lim← G/N; it is used instead of Mathlib's ProfiniteGrp category limits to keep the statement elementary.

δ(G) (profiniteRank) is ℕ∞-valued: the infimum of |S| over finite subsets S ⊆ Ĝ whose generated subgroup is topologically dense in Ĝ. The API lemma profiniteRank_le_rank (proved in the file) shows δ(G) ≤ d(G) < ⊤ for finitely generated G, so the ⊤ junk value never occurs in the theorem. The hypothesis δ(G) = n is stated as profiniteRank G = (n : ℕ∞).

The question 'Is d bounded on the set of groups with the fixed value of δ(G) ≥ 2?' is read, following the decomposition table, as: for every n ≥ 2 there exists C with d(G) ≤ C for all finitely generated residually finite G with δ(G) = n. answer(True) is a positive answer; answer(False) means for some n ≥ 2 the rank d is unbounded on that class.
Residual finiteness is defined element-wise (every non-identity element avoids some normal subgroup of finite index), which is the standard textbook definition and equivalent to injectivity of G → Ĝ.
d(G) is Mathlib's Group.rank G, which requires the [Group.FG G] hypothesis; finite generation of G is thus an instance hypothesis, matching 'Let G be a finitely generated ... group'.
Groups are quantified over Type (universe 0), following the convention of the other Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 20_76).

Scoped instances put the discrete topology on each finite quotient G ⧸ N (N a finite-index normal subgroup) and supply the Normal/FiniteIndex instances from the subtype property; they are scoped to the namespace Kourovka.«6.31» to avoid any global instance diamonds.
Noskov's cited existence of groups with d(G) > δ(G) is recorded in the module docstring as background only, not formalised, per the decomposition table.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity: 'Is d bounded on the set of groups with the fixed value of δ(G) ≥ 2' has an implicit outer quantifier over the fixed value; a single uniform bound over all δ ≥ 2 is impossible (d ≥ δ), so the per-n reading (∀ n ≥ 2, ∃ C(n)) used by all candidates is the only sensible one. Mathlib has no residual-finiteness or profinite-completion-of-abstract-group notion, so bespoke definitions were unavoidable; they are kept in the problem file (a maintainer may prefer moving profiniteCompletion/profiniteRank to FormalConjecturesForMathlib). Noskov's cited result is background and not formalized. c02 and c08 named the theorem `parts.b` rather than the slot name `kourovka.«6.31».parts.b`; the chosen c01 follows the existing Kourovka idiom. Residual finiteness is stated via finite-index normal subgroups (equivalent to the homomorphism-to-finite-group formulation used by c03/c04/c08).
statement:
b) Let $G$ be a finitely generated residually finite group, $d(G)$ the minimal number of its generators, and $\delta (G)$ the minimal number of topological generators of the profinite completion of $G$. It is known that there exist groups $G$ for which $d(G) > \delta
(G)$ (G. A. Noskov, Math. Notes, 33, no. 4 (1983), 249–254). Is the function $d$ bounded on the set of groups $G$ with the fixed value of $\delta (G) \geq 2$?
